sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: In a trial of 1,137 adults with resected melanoma, the personalised mRNA vaccine intismeran combined with the immunotherapy drug pembrolizumab cut the risk of cancer returning or death by 42% after two years. Additionally, 82% of patients receiving the combined treatment remained alive and recurrence-free, compared with 70% taking immunotherapy alone.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: It is the first individualised cancer vaccine to show positive phase III trial results. The vaccine targets up to 34 unique genetic mutations from a patient's tumour to train the immune system to prevent cancer returning.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Results will be presented at a Madrid conference and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Manufacturers MSD and Moderna are seeking regulatory approval and testing the vaccine against lung, bladder and kidney cancers.
